articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft's April patch bonanza fixes 167 vulnerabilities including a SharePoint zero-day and the deliciously-named 'BlueHammer' Windows Defender flaw. When your monthly security update looks like a CVE phone book, maybe it's time to reconsider your development practices.

articles.title: The Internet Still Works: SmugMug Powers Online Photography
articles.summary: EFF calls out Congress for serving up another surveillance state appetizer disguised as 'accountability.' Speaker Johnson's new FISA 702 bill is apparently just lipstick on the warrantless spying pig.

articles.title: EFF Challenges Secrecy In Eastern District of Texas Patent Case
articles.summary: California wants to ban social media for under-16s while forcing everyone to verify their identity first. Because nothing says 'protecting kids' like creating a state-mandated digital ID system that would make Xi Jinping jealous.

articles.title: 20-Year-Old Malware Rewrites History of Cyber Sabotage
articles.summary: Researchers discover 'PhantomRPC' - an architectural flaw in Windows RPC that offers five different paths to privilege escalation. It's like Microsoft built a choose-your-own-adventure book for local admin access.

articles.title: Parsing Agentic Offensive Security's Existential Threat
articles.summary: Meet 'fast16' - malware that predates Stuxnet by five years, rewriting the timeline of sophisticated cyber sabotage. Turns out the digital warfare arms race started even earlier than we thought.

articles.title: CIA Ran MK-ULTRA Experiments on Prisoners of War in U.S. Custody, Declassified Docs Confirm
articles.summary: Four Democrats hold the keys to Trump's domestic surveillance kingdom, and advocates are watching to see if they'll hand over warrantless spying powers. Democracy hanging by the votes of four people - what could go wrong?

articles.title: Kash Patel Got Arrested for Public Urination After a Night of Drinking
articles.summary: Declassified docs finally confirm the CIA ran MK-ULTRA experiments on North Korean POWs in US custody. Nothing like a good FOIA win to remind us that conspiracy theories sometimes undersell government fuckery.

articles.title: Microsoft Patches Entra ID Role Flaw That Enabled Service Principal Takeover
articles.summary: Home security giant ADT got digitally burgled by ShinyHunters, who claim 10 million records while ADT insists it was just a 'limited set.' The irony is so thick you could cut it with a compromised smart lock.

articles.title: Checkmarx Confirms GitHub Repository Data Posted on Dark Web After March 23 Attack
articles.summary: Microsoft admits CVE-2026-32202 in Windows Shell is being actively exploited after initially downplaying it. Nothing builds confidence like a vendor going 'oops, that spoofing vulnerability is actually being used to spoof people.'

articles.title: Flowtriq Detects 48.3 Gbps Multi-Vector DDoS Attack in Under One Second
articles.summary: Claude Mythos Preview is finding vulnerabilities faster than teams can remediate them, fundamentally changing the math of disclosure. When AI can pwn your infrastructure faster than humans can patch it, we've entered a very interesting new era.
